extraction.name: VQAonline
extraction.description: The first Visual Question Answering (VQA) dataset in which all contents originate from an authentic use case, sourced from Stack Exchange online question answering community forums. It contains 64,696 visual questions spanning 105 diverse topics across five super-categories, where each example includes an authentic natural language question, supplementary context, an image, and an answer validated as acceptable by the individual asking the question.
extraction.creator: Chongyan Chen, Mengchen Liu, Noel Codella, Yunsheng Li, Lu Yuan, Danna Gurari
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected by scraping publicly available archives of the online question-answering platform Stack Exchange hosted at Internet Archive (https://archive.org/details/stackexchange). Examples were selected if they contained a natural language question (post title), natural language context (body text), an image (URL link), and at least one 'accepted answer' marked by the user who posted the question. 75 technology topics were excluded, leaving 105 topical sites.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Started with 330,705 candidate visual questions. After removing visual questions without an accepted answer, 165,766 remained. Filtering out posts with scores <= 0 left 119,177. Removing questions with multiple images left 85,573. Removing questions with visual answers left 65,849. Finally, removing examples for which the image could not be downloaded from the provided link yielded the final dataset of 64,696 visual questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Publicly available Stack Exchange data dump hosted at https://archive.org/details/stackexchange in XML format.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were converted to PNG format for data format consistency. Filtering removed questions without accepted answers, visual questions with score 0 or less for either question or answer, visual questions with multiple images, visual questions with visual answers, and instances where the image URL was broken.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations (visual questions, context, answers, accepted status) originate authentically from Stack Exchange platform users. For user intent labeling on a subset of 105 examples (one per topic), three crowdworkers from Amazon Mechanical Turk categorized intent into eight categories (instruction, evidence, verification, advice, identification, opinion, reason, other) based on definitions and examples. Additionally, domain expert evaluations were collected from 10 experts who each rated model-generated answers on 20 VQAs within their topic as correct (1), partially correct (0.5), or incorrect (0).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (for user intent annotation) and a home-grown, web-based interface (for expert qualitative evaluation, code available at https://github.com/VQAonline/VQAonlineVisualization).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For user intention taxonomy development, two authors annotated 105 visual questions over four rounds; Cohen's kappa agreement improved from 45.24% to 84.69% and agreement accuracy from 53.3% to 87.5%. For crowdworkers on MTurk, two independent workers labeled each instance, and if they disagreed (25 out of 105 instances), a third worker was hired to break the tie using majority vote. For expert evaluation, domain experts' time per question was inspected (median 1.4 minutes, mean 1.29 minutes) to verify attention.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: For user intention: 2 to 3 crowdworkers per item (majority vote). For expert qualitative evaluation: 1 domain expert per evaluated item (rating 6 model answers each).
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: User intention crowdworkers: 3 workers located in the United States with >500 HITs and >95% approval rating on Amazon Mechanical Turk. Expert annotators: 10 domain experts located in the United States, each with at least a Master's degree in a field related to their assigned VQA topic.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: DeepSolo (used for text spotting / detection within dataset images), GPT-3.5 (used in preliminary bootstrapping of user intention categories), and LLaMA2 (used as an automated text correctness evaluation metric).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Models developed for VQAonline can benefit real-world applications including community question answering platforms (e.g., Yahoo! Answers, Quora), learning assistance VQA tools for children, virtual assistants, visual dialog and query, and visual search/browsing. User intention modeling facilitates creating human-centered VQA models tailored to user needs.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas since VQAs are posted by Stack Exchange users with access to mobile devices and Internet. The geographic representation of Stack Exchange is unbalanced, with more posts coming from countries like the US, India, and European countries, and fewer from countries like Egypt. Additionally, 52% of all VQAs belong to only 23% of the topics (science topics).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Answers are much longer (mean 173 words) and paragraph-form, rendering standard short-answer VQA metrics ineffective. Modern VLMs perform poorly and struggle with reasoning, fine-grained understanding, and distinguishing images when language context is strong (leading to hallucinations). The presence of text in 76% of images creates challenges for multilingual text recognition.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Visual Question Answering training, validation, testing, few-shot learning, and benchmarking; research into long-form multimodal QA, multilingual VQA, text VQA, multimodal hallucination, and evaluation metric alignment.
